Module golang.org/x/mod v0.41.0 (BSD-3-Clause); the code is package sumdb/tlog, and every sources path is relative to the module root. Hashing, tree shape and proofs follow RFC 9162 section 2.1 exactly: leaf SHA-256(0x00 || data), node SHA-256(0x01 || left || right), split at the largest power of two strictly smaller than n (maxpow2), no padding, no duplicated odd node, audit path bottom to top. CheckRecord is recursive rather than the RFC 9162 2.1.3.2 bit loop, but it is equivalent: it rejects t < 0, n < 0 and n >= t, and it fails on any missing or extra path hash. This file's Go program checks this against an independent RFC 9162 reference (MTH, PATH, the 2.1.3.2 verifier) written with crypto/sha256 only: MTH vs TreeHash and PATH vs ProveRecord for every index of every fixture tree and of every upstream TestTree size 1..100, and verifier agreement on every inclusion case, every upstream corruption over sizes 1..100, and structural mutations (index = size, size + 1, extra hash, dropped first or last hash, reversed path, sibling index). They all agree, so deviations is empty and no case carries rfc9162_valid.

Tree size 0: TreeHash(0, r) returns SHA-256("") = e3b0c442...b855 (the emptyHash literal at tlog.go:237-244), not a zero hash, and it never calls the reader (TreeHash(0, nil) works). The fixture carries it both as empty_root and as a tree of size 0. ProveRecord(t=0, n) and CheckRecord(p, t=0, ...) both return "tlog: invalid inputs", so no inclusion proof exists for an empty tree; the tree_size 0 edge cases below record CheckRecord's answer, which is always invalid. At the other end, tlog cannot work with more than 2^62 leaves: maxpow2 (sumdb/tlog/tlog.go:70-78) never returns for n above 2^62, since 1<<63 is negative and 1<<64 is 0 in int64. CheckRecord therefore does not return for a tree_size above 2^62 once leaf_index is in range and the path is not empty (it still answers at once for an index out of range or an empty path), and ProveRecord and TreeHash, which split with the same helper, do not return at such sizes either. No case here comes near that size, and the program never hands tlog such a size read from a file.

Published answers are few. TestTree in tlog_test.go derives nothing from hard-coded values: it only compares tlog's own code paths with each other (StoredHashes/TreeHash, ProveRecord/CheckRecord, and the tile readers). The hard-coded answers are: the empty hash; RecordHash("hello world") in note_test.go; the SECURITY ERROR text recorded in a comment in sumdb/client_test.go TestClientFork (lines 116-139); and the all-zero starting tree hash of TestClientBadTiles (client_test.go:83-92). The SECURITY ERROR text gives the roots of four trees over the test log's record texts (sizes 4, 5, 5 and 6; line 148 asserts a prefix of the tc2 size 5 root), two leaf hashes, and a consistency proof ProveTree(6, 5) = [leaf 4, leaf 5, MTH(D[0:4])]. All reproduce with tlog. The schema has no consistency section, so that proof is not a fixture entry; its three elements appear as hash_checks and as the size 4 tree root, and the program confirms that tlog.ProveTree(6, 5) reproduces it, that CheckTree accepts it for tc2's roots, and that CheckTree rejects tc's forked size 5 root. The comment's line 121 reads "go.sum database tree!" with a stray "!"; the asserted text at line 144 has none, and the hash on line 123 reproduces. TestClientBadTiles hands the client a signed tree of size 1 whose hash is tlog.Hash{} (32 zero bytes) and requires the lookup to fail; upstream detects it through tile hashes, not CheckRecord. It is the one published inclusion case: record 0 of newTestClient (the only leaf of a size 1 tree) at index 0, empty path, the all-zero root, upstream_expectation invalid, and CheckRecord rejects it. Its valid counterpart is the generated tree of size 1 that newTestClient signs at client_test.go:306 (root = RecordHash(record 0)) and that tree's one proof.

How the client_test.go cases are labeled. Upstream's client tests never call tlog.CheckRecord. They assert inclusion through sumdb.Client, which reads a record's stored hash through tlog.TileHashReader, whose tiles must hash to the signed tree hash (sumdb/tlog/tile.go:398-417). Client.checkRecord (sumdb/client.go:479-495) compares that hash, read from the client's latest tree, with RecordHash of the record data, and Client init checks the configured signed tree against its own tiles through checkTrees (client.go:153-161, 320-333 and 430-442). A lookup that upstream requires to succeed therefore asserts exactly the statement an inclusion case encodes (leaf leaf_index of the tree of tree_size with this root), and a signed tree that upstream requires the client to reject asserts its negation. So each client_test.go case is labeled by what upstream requires of the client: "valid" where a lookup that must succeed authenticates that record in that tree, "invalid" for the one tree the client must reject (TestClientBadTiles lines 83-92, where init fails with "checking tree#1: downloaded inconsistent tile"), and "none" for every other proof, which no upstream line decides. Each labeled case's name ends with the upstream lines. The valid ones are: record 0 in the signed tree of size 1 (Client init before the first lookup at lines 30, 73, 103, 109 and 232); records 2 and 0 in the size 3 tree (lines 30-31 and 72-73; lines 42-43, where the response carries tree 1 but the client's latest tree is 3); record 3 in the size 4 tree (lines 49-50 and 80-81); tc's record 4 in tc's size 5 tree (line 103); tc2's record 5 in tc2's size 6 tree (line 109); and record 4 in the TestRejectUnauthenticatedLines size 5 tree (lines 232-235). The program replays each of these clients with tlog alone. It publishes each test log's tiles as addRecord does (client_test.go:402-411, tile height 2), runs init, mergeLatest's checkTrees and checkRecord through tlog.TileHashReader, and requires every upstream outcome, including the ErrSecurity of TestClientFork lines 111-114. It takes the labels from that replay, once over the upstream records and once over the fixture's own trees, and CheckRecord agrees with every label.

Client trees. Besides the four published trees, the fixture holds newTestClient's signed trees of size 1, 2 and 3 (signTree at client_test.go:306, and at line 400 as records 1 and 2 are added) and the TestRejectUnauthenticatedLines tree of size 5 (records 0..3 and the record at line 195, TreeHash at line 209), with every proof over each. No upstream line states their roots, so they are generated. The size 2 tree is served only with the lookup of record 1, which no test makes, so its proofs are all "none".

No upstream file hard-codes an inclusion proof path, so every other inclusion case is generated with tlog.ProveRecord and tlog.NodeHash, and valid comes from tlog.CheckRecord. "generated: ProveRecord over published ..." cases cover every index of the four published client_test trees, labeled as described above; for tc2's size 6 tree at indexes 4 and 5, and tc2's size 5 tree at index 4, every path element and the root are published literals. "generated: ... TestTree" cases use the upstream leaf data "leaf %d": all proofs for sizes 1..16 (upstream asserts valid) and, for each, every upstream corruption p[k][0] ^= 1, named after the upstream failure message "corrupt proof hash #k" (upstream asserts invalid). Upstream runs sizes 1..100. To keep the file small the fixture carries trees for sizes 1..16 and 100 and proofs for sizes 1..16; the program still runs the whole 1..100 range, with every upstream corruption, without storing it.

Edge cases (579, names "generated: edge \"<kind>\": ..."), for the classes upstream never asks CheckRecord about. All are built over the TestTree leaf data for tree sizes 1..16 with tlog's own functions, all have upstream_expectation none, and CheckRecord rejects every one; the RFC 9162 2.1.3.2 reference agrees on each. The kinds, and how many cases a verifier missing one rule would accept (so that rule alone rejects them): "index = tree_size" (16: the last leaf's own proof and root, leaf_index set to tree_size; the RFC loop without its index check accepts 1, an index-bit fold that ignores tree_size and path length accepts 7). "index >= tree_size, low bits kept" (136: every leaf's own proof and root, leaf_index m + 2^K for 2^K the smallest power of two >= tree_size; the RFC loop without its index check accepts 117, the index-bit fold 117). "index >= tree_size, int64 max" (16: the last leaf's proof and root, leaf_index 2^63 - 1; 5 and 16). "tree_size 0" (4: empty path with leaf = root = SHA-256(""), empty path with leaf = root = RecordHash("leaf 0"), empty path with root SHA-256(""), and the size 2 proof of leaf 0 with tree_size 0; the index-bit fold accepts 3, the RFC loop without its index check 0, since sn = -1 never reaches 0). "path one short" (135: ProveRecord's path with its top element dropped, root = the TreeHash of the child subtree of the top split that holds the leaf; CheckRecord accepts 135 of these shortened paths as proofs inside that subtree, the RFC loop without its length rules accepts 135, the index-bit fold 129. In 50 of them the leaf is in the right subtree and the RFC loop runs out of path with fn == sn != 0, the right-edge termination class). "path one long, extra hash folded on the left" (136: ProveRecord's path plus RecordHash("leaf n") on top, root NodeHash(extra, TreeHash(n)), which is what a verifier that keeps folding past the top computes; the RFC loop without its length rules accepts 136). "path one long, extra hash folded on the right" (136: the same path, root NodeHash(TreeHash(n), extra); 31 of them, those with n a power of two, equal TreeHash(n + 1) and ProveRecord(n + 1, m), the size n + 1 proof with tree_size understated; the index-bit fold accepts 117).

Every entry name starts with "published:" (the value is an upstream literal: empty_root, 6 hash_checks, 5 trees, 1 inclusion case), "generated:" (produced by tlog over upstream leaf data: 21 trees and 1214 inclusion cases) or "derived:" (2 hash_checks, SHA-256 values computed from upstream leaf data or published hashes that no upstream file states). upstream_expectation is "valid" on 143 cases, "invalid" on 469 and "none" on 603. Leaf data here is variable length (record texts, "leaf %d"), so a 32-byte-leaf API should use leaf_hashes and treat leaf_data as provenance.
